body.value:
1. [... ... ] Yeshu [ ...
  2. ... th]eir names [are Matai and Na]qi and Buni [and Netzer and Todah ... ]

  3. [... R.] Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah. He said to Matai: “[Why is] your [name called] Matai?” He said [to him: “Because about me]

  4. David [said], ‘[Matai (=When)] will I come and be seen before God?’.” He said to him: “F[oo]l! No! Thus said D[avid]

  5. about you, ‘[Matai (=when) will he die] and his name perish’!” And he decreed upon him, and they strangled him. Th[ey brought Na]qi. He (Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah) said to him: “[Why i]s

  6. your name called Naqi?” He said to him: “About me [David] said, ‘Neqi (=The one who has clean) [hands] and a p[ure hea]rt’.”

  7. He said to [Naqi: “F]ool! No, for the Bible said about you, ‘and He (God) shall naqe not yenaqe (=shall by no means absolve (the sin))’.” And it was ordered ab[out him and they th]rew him into a

  8. [fie]ry furnace. [... ...] Buni. [He (Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah) said: “Why are] you called Buni?” He said to him: “Because about me the Bible says,

  9. ‘Israel is [beni (=my son), the firstborn]’.” [R. Ye]hosh[uʿa ben Peraḥiah] sa[id to him: “Foo]l! Thus says the Bible about you,

  10. ‘Behold I [will kill] binkha (=your son), the firstbo[rn’.” And it was ordered] about him and they stoned him. And after him he (i.e., Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah) summoned Netzer. He said: “And why 

  11. [is your name called Netzer?” He said to hi]m: “For about me the Bible says, ‘and a netzer (=sprout) will grow from its roots’.” He said to him: “Fool! Thus

  12. the Bi[ble said a]bo[ut you], ‘you were cast out of your tomb like a detested netzer (=sprout)’.” And it was decreed upon him,

  13. and his head was cut off. After him they brought Todah. He (Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah) said to him: “Why is your name called Todah?” He said to him:

  14. “For about me David said, “A psalm for todah (=thanksgiving)’.” He said to him: “Fool! Thus said David about you, ‘He who sacrifices todah (=a thanksgiving offering) honors me’.”

  15. And it was decreed upon him, and they executed him. Pilatus the governor answered R. Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah: “The five

  16. disciples of Yeshu the wicked who misled the wo[rl]d have been executed, and Yoḥanan the Dyer—

  17. Yeshu’s teacher—and he (Yeshu) deserve to be executed.” R. Yehoshuʿa answered and said to Pilatus: “If our master wishes,

  18. we shall send and inform [Tibe]rinus Caesar and whatever he shall tell us, we shall do.” They sent to him:

  19. “There are seven men here, who misled the whole world and such is their business”— everything they had been doing.

  20. [When] King Tiberinus Caesar [he]ard, he sent: “Bring them tome!”And they brought them to him.

  21. And Aligus (?) the governor and Marinus the great elder, [and R.] Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah and Rabbi [Yehud]ah

  22. the [gardener] we[nt] with them to Tiberias, the great town. And they all went before Tiberinus Caesar.

  23. And when [Yoḥanan] the Dyer and Yeshu [came] before him, [Tiber]inus Caesar said to them: “What is [your] business [and who are you?]?”

  24. They answered and said to him that “We ar[e] the sons of the G[od] of Heaven; and [thes]e boo[ks] 

  25. that are in our hand are not ours.” He said to them: “And where are they from?” [They said to hi]m:

  26. “They are [books of] heal[ing], and every person who needs healing, we he[al] him, and if [we want] to revive [we revive and if we want]

  27. to kill we kill, and everything we want to do—we do.

  28. [And a] barren [woman] who did not give birth and is suffering—we can give her a child (even) without (intercourse with) a man.

  29. And also, whoever his soul [is about] to come out, and if he is about to die, we whisper [in his ear? and...].

  30. And if we want to... 

[Caesar said... “I do not ask] of you [ . . . . . . can you grant her a son without] a man?” Yeshu answered and said: “Y[es].” [ ... ... ] Yeshu [whispered?] words of magic, and she became pregnant. [Caesar] ans[wered]
